newsitem.title: UK: Cash Brent holds steadier levels, wet market soft.
newsitem.headline: Cash Brent holds steadier levels, wet market soft.

text.p: North Sea crude paper was talked around the day's highs on Thursday afternoon following a morning rally on news of smaller than expected Brent April loading programmes, traders said.
But wet Brent differentials continued to be discussed at the equivalent of recently traded levels around April Brent -60 cents.
April Brent crude futures traded at $20.00 a barrel at 1721 GMT, 39 cents higher on the day and steady from morning levels.
April/May Brent was talked around +32/37 cents and May/June was +7/9 cents.
This followed a morning trade at +32/+33 cents, a 13-cent rise on news the Brent programme would be the equivalent of eight full cargoes lighter than in March.
While scheduled maintenance at fields in the Brent and Ninian systems had been expected to cut volumes, the shutdowns could not account for the entire shortfall, traders said.
Dated Brent was bid at April -70 cents and continued to be offered at the equivalent of April Brent -60 cents on Thursday, the lower end of Wednesday's range.
A Brent cargo loading March 28-30, the only Brent nominated from the paper chains, was kept ahead of the five o'clock deadline by Stasco. The final three March Brents will turn wet on Friday.
An Ekofisk loading March 28/30 went at Dated -5 cents but traders said inclusion of a seller's option incidated the level was not markedly weaker than the previous trade of +14 cents.

CFDs were unchanged to slightly weaker from morning levels. Next week was talked around May -25/-22 cents after morning assessments of -25/-19 cents. March 24-27 was at May -23/-20 after May -21/-17 cents.
